public_rationale: CNBC reported OpenAI's March 31, 2025 announcement of a $40 billion round as the largest individual private-tech funding round on record [e1]. SoftBank's April 1 disclosure described its own expected investment as up to $30 billion after planned syndication [e2]. Neither item establishes OpenAI's total financing requirement as of May 27, 2025 or a historical maximum for cumulative investment in one startup on matching terms, so the comparison remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: A record individual funding round does not establish a record for cumulative startup investment.
The evidence does not quantify OpenAI's total financing requirement or define its funding horizon.
The evidence does not provide a historical comparison with consistent treatment of equity, debt, secondary sales, commitments and cash invested.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI needs more money than has ever been invested in a startup.

statement.excerpt: On top of that, it requires more money than has ever been invested in a startup.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading compares OpenAI's financing requirement known at the post date with the largest cumulative investment previously made in any single startup.
I do not silently replace cumulative investment with the largest individual funding round.
The comparison concerns the financing requirement understood at the post date, not requirements announced later.
The statement does not quantify the requirement, define a funding horizon, or identify an accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: A documented OpenAI financing requirement exceeds a reliable historical maximum for cumulative capital invested in an individual startup, using consistent treatment of equity, debt, commitments, and completed investments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reliable historical example of cumulative startup investment equals or exceeds the documented OpenAI requirement on the same basis.
